title: CONGENITAL FIBROSIS OF EXTRAOCULAR MUSCLES 3A, SYNDROMIC 2, WITH JOINT CONTRACTURES, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY, AND PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY

relationships.phenotype: CONGENITAL FIBROSIS OF EXTRAOCULAR MUSCLES 3A, SYNDROMIC 2, WITH JOINT CONTRACTURES, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY, AND PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that syndromic congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles-3A with joint contractures, developmental delay, and peripheral neuropathy (CFEOM3A2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TUBB3 gene (602661) on chromosome 16q24.

checks.claim: Syndromic congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles-3A with joint contractures, developmental delay, and peripheral neuropathy (CFEOM3A2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TUBB3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we now report that 8 different heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3, also known as TuJ1, result in CFEOM3 in isolation or as a component of several previously undefined neurological syndromes.
checks.explanation: Syndromic CFEOM3 with contractures, developmental delay and neuropathy caused by heterozygous TUBB3 mutations is described; the CFEOM3A2 label is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The TUBB3 gene is located on chromosome 16q24.
checks.evidence_quote: TUBB3 c.785G>A variant (NM_006086.4; Chr16:89935236 (hg38); Arg262His)
checks.explanation: The paper gives a chromosome 16 coordinate. The band 16q24 is standard nomenclature for this gene's location.

paragraphs.text: CFEOM3A2 is a syndromic form of congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles caused by specific heterozygous missense mutations in the neuron-specific beta-tubulin isotype III gene TUBB3. Affected individuals have congenital restrictive ophthalmoplegia with ptosis, usually with additional features such as congenital joint contractures, developmental delay or intellectual disability, and a later-onset axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy.

checks.claim: CFEOM3A2 is a syndromic form of congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles.
checks.evidence_quote: result in CFEOM3 in isolation or as a component of several previously undefined neurological syndromes.
checks.explanation: Syndromic forms of CFEOM3 are described.

checks.claim: CFEOM3A2 is caused by specific heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3.
checks.evidence_quote: We report that eight heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3, encoding the neuron-specific beta-tubulin isotype III, result in a spectrum of human nervous system disorders that we now call the TUBB3 syndromes.
checks.explanation: Specific heterozygous missense mutations (e.g., R262H, D417H, E410K) cause syndromic phenotypes.

checks.claim: TUBB3 encodes the neuron-specific beta-tubulin isotype III.
checks.evidence_quote: TUBB3, encoding the neuron-specific beta-tubulin isotype III

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A2 have congenital restrictive ophthalmoplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: affected individuals are born with blepharoptosis (drooping eyelids) and restricted eye movements.
checks.explanation: Congenital restricted eye movements = restrictive ophthalmoplegia.

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A2 have ptosis.
checks.evidence_quote: affected individuals are born with blepharoptosis (drooping eyelids) and restricted eye movements.

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A2 usually have congenital joint contractures.
checks.evidence_quote: Thirteen subjects have congenital and one has acquired contractures of distal joints of varying severity.
checks.explanation: Thirteen of 14 subjects had congenital contractures, which supports 'usually'.

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A2 usually have developmental delay or intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: All fourteen subjects have varying degrees of global developmental delay

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A2 usually develop a later-onset axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Most subjects harboring D417N and the oldest patient harboring E410K developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the second to third decade, all in the absence of congenital contractures
checks.explanation: Neuropathy onset varies by mutation (first decade for R262H/D417H); paper supports axonal sensorimotor neuropathy but not uniformly 'later-onset' in syndromic cases.

paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) described patients with TUBB3 mutations who had CFEOM3 together with additional features. Some substitutions were associated with syndromic phenotypes that included congenital joint contractures, facial weakness, developmental delay or intellectual disability, and a progressive axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy that developed later in life.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) described patients with TUBB3 mutations who had CFEOM3 together with additional features.
checks.evidence_quote: Each mutation causes the ocular motility disorder CFEOM3, whereas some also result in intellectual and behavioral impairments, facial paralysis, and/or later-onset axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.

checks.claim: Some TUBB3 substitutions were associated with syndromic phenotypes that included congenital joint contractures.
checks.evidence_quote: All subjects harboring D417H or R262H were born with congenital wrist and finger contractures

checks.claim: Some TUBB3 substitutions were associated with syndromic phenotypes that included facial weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas all participants with R262H, E410K, and D417H had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness

checks.claim: Some TUBB3 substitutions were associated with syndromic phenotypes that included developmental delay or intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Individuals with A302T, E410K, R262H, and R380C had more severe CC dysgenesis and mild to moderate intellectual, social, and behavioral impairments.

checks.claim: Some TUBB3 substitutions were associated with syndromic phenotypes that included a progressive axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy that developed later in life.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas some also result in intellectual and behavioral impairments, facial paralysis, and/or later-onset axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
checks.explanation: Stated; text also describes it as progressive.

paragraphs.text: The syndromic TUBB3 phenotypes are caused by heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance; many reported cases resulted from de novo mutations (Tischfield et al., 2010).

checks.claim: The syndromic TUBB3 phenotypes are caused by heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified TUBB3 as the mutated gene underlying a series of autosomal dominant disorders of axon guidance that we collectively call the TUBB3 syndromes.

checks.claim: Many reported cases of syndromic TUBB3 phenotypes resulted from de novo mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: while the TUBB3 phenotypes limited to CFEOM3 and polyneuropathy often segregate in autosomal dominant families, those with more severe clinical findings typically arise de novo.

paragraphs.text: Mutations in TUBB3 cause a spectrum of disorders. Some missense mutations cause isolated or nearly isolated CFEOM3A, whereas other, recurrent amino acid substitutions are associated with syndromic phenotypes that include neurologic and other systemic features. TUBB3 mutations are also associated with malformations of cortical development.

checks.claim: Mutations in TUBB3 cause a spectrum of disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: result in a spectrum of human nervous system disorders that we now call the TUBB3 syndromes.

checks.claim: Some TUBB3 missense mutations cause isolated or nearly isolated CFEOM3A.
checks.evidence_quote: Overall, most adults with isolated CFEOM3 have R262C or, less commonly, R62Q or A302T substitutions.

checks.claim: Other, recurrent TUBB3 amino acid substitutions are associated with syndromic phenotypes that include neurologic and other systemic features.
checks.evidence_quote: six others (Gly71Arg, Gly98Ser, Arg262His, Arg380Cis, Glu410Lys, Asp417His) are more likely to arise de novo and be associated with more severe neurological phenotypes
checks.explanation: Recurrence is shown by R262H appearing in 13 unrelated families. The syndromic features include neurological and endocrine involvement.

checks.claim: TUBB3 mutations are associated with malformations of cortical development.
checks.evidence_quote: A separate set of missense mutations in TUBB3 cause malformations of cortical development (MCD) along with other brain abnormalities, but without CFEOM3

paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified heterozygous missense mutations in the TUBB3 gene in patients with CFEOM3, including both isolated and syndromic forms. Functional studies showed that the mutations altered microtubule dynamics and kinesin interactions, and a knockin mouse model carrying a human mutation showed defects in axon guidance of cranial nerves and of the anterior commissure and corpus callosum.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3 in patients with CFEOM3, including both isolated and syndromic forms.
checks.evidence_quote: we now report that 8 different heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3, also known as TuJ1, result in CFEOM3 in isolation or as a component of several previously undefined neurological syndromes.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Tischfield et al. (2010) showed that TUBB3 mutations altered microtubule dynamics.
checks.evidence_quote: Modeling each mutation in yeast tubulin demonstrates that all alter dynamic instability whereas a subset disrupts the interaction of microtubules with kinesin motors.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Tischfield et al. (2010) showed that TUBB3 mutations altered kinesin interactions.
checks.evidence_quote: Modeling each mutation in yeast tubulin demonstrates that all alter dynamic instability whereas a subset disrupts the interaction of microtubules with kinesin motors.

checks.claim: A knockin mouse model carrying a human TUBB3 mutation showed defects in axon guidance of cranial nerves.
checks.evidence_quote: Tubb3R262C/R262C mice showed defects in the guidance of commissural axons and cranial nerves.

checks.claim: A knockin mouse model carrying a human TUBB3 mutation showed defects in axon guidance of the anterior commissure and corpus callosum.
checks.evidence_quote: There was significant thinning and/or absent midline crossing of the AC throughout its anterior-posterior axis compared to WT mice
checks.explanation: AC defects and CC agenesis with Probst bundles in 2/5 homozygous mice reported.

paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) proposed that TUBB3 mutations cause a disorder of axon guidance, in which abnormal microtubule dynamics and impaired interactions with kinesin motors disrupt the guidance of developing axons, including oculomotor nerve fibers that innervate the extraocular muscles.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) proposed that TUBB3 mutations cause a disorder of axon guidance.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified TUBB3 as the mutated gene underlying a series of autosomal dominant disorders of axon guidance that we collectively call the TUBB3 syndromes.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) proposed that abnormal microtubule dynamics and impaired interactions with kinesin motors caused by TUBB3 mutations disrupt the guidance of developing axons, including oculomotor nerve fibers that innervate the extraocular muscles.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, reduced Tubb3 microtubule incorporation and/or the residual mutant protein affect the ability of Kif21a to interact with microtubules and may contribute to oculomotor nerve misguidance in mice and humans.
checks.explanation: Paper links altered dynamics and kinesin interactions to axon guidance defects, including oculomotor nerve.
